title.narrative: Sustainable Waste Management for Sierra Leone

description.narrative: At the macro level, the project will work with the Ministry of Local Government and Community Affairs, the Ministry of Health, the Ministry of Environment, National Public Procurement Authority and the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry and the Environmental Protection Agency. These public institutions will be crucial to the successful implementation of drafted waste management srategy in Phase 1 and revise the existing green procurement policy. At the meso level, the project will work with 5 city councils and relevant universities in those cities, and with SMEs operating in the waste management. University of Sierra Leone in Freetown; Eastern Technical University in Kenema; Government Technical Institute in Koidu City; Manjama Agricultural Institute in Bo City. Their human resource capacity for waste management will be enhanced. In addition, knowledge, skills and technology will be transferred from these institutions to SMEs and communities. In the meantime, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in waste management will be provided with technical capacity to convert solid waste-to-wealth through recycling of plastic and composting of biodegradable wastes.At the micro level, people in urban and peri-urban areas will be engaged in waste segregation at household level and youth group provide waste collection service to the community. In addition, the community will get recycled products and compost directly from the SMEs.WHH is working with four civil society organizations: In Bo this will be Action for Community Development & Good Governance (ACDG), in Makeni - Sierra Leone Citizens Rights & Association (SLCRA), in Koidu - Knowledge for Community Empowerment Organization (KoCEPO) and in Kenema - Movement for Restoration of Democracy (MRD) which are all partners from phase 1, new partners will be identified for Freetown.

Overall objective is to improve communal waste management structures and policies in Sierra Leone through fair and inclusive Ecologization of the economy and the creation of decent work and income opportunities for women and youth.

WHH has been engaged in solid waste management since 2013 in Sierra Leone by constructing landfill site in Bo city as a pilot and rollout and expand the intervention areas to Kenema, Makeni and Koidu cities until 2023. The second phase of the project entitled “Sustainable Waste Management for Sierra Leone” will strengthening the policy improvement and privet sector involvement in waste management. In addition, the system strengthening is crucial for the foundation to introducing circular economy approach to waste management sector in Sierra Leone cities and shift the current linear system, take-make-waste. Therefore, a wide range of stakeholders will be participated in policy development, implementation and improvement of waste management value-chain and practices.
